headline: BIR Files ₱2.23-Billion Tax Case Against Hongsheng Gaming Technology
seoTitle: BIR Files ₱2.23B Tax Case Against Hongsheng | FMB News
seoDescription: The Bureau of Internal Revenue filed a roughly ₱2.23-billion tax evasion case against offshore gaming operator Hongsheng Gaming Technology Inc.
deck: Revenue authorities filed a multibillion-peso tax case against the offshore gaming operator as the government continues enforcement against former POGO entities.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bureau of Internal Revenue filed a tax evasion case worth about ₱2.23 billion against Hongsheng Gaming Technology Inc., an offshore gaming operator associated with the Bamban, Tarlac POGO compound.

The approved FMB News brief places the complaint before the Department of Justice and says the assessment covers alleged unpaid taxes and related liabilities. Contemporary reporting independently corroborates a BIR case of approximately ₱2.23 billion against Hongsheng.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Offshore gaming operations have been banned in the Philippines, but closure does not erase outstanding tax liabilities. BIR Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 13-2026 states that former POGOs and related entities remain liable for taxes, duties, regulatory fees and other charges up to their last day of operations and may still be audited.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The filing tests the government's ability to recover tax liabilities from companies linked to the now-banned offshore gaming sector and to pursue corporate officers where the law allows.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next step is the Justice Department's evaluation of the complaint and any preliminary investigation. A tax complaint is an allegation and does not by itself establish criminal liability.
